Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1070
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1070
- **Title**: fix(#1066): wait out transient rate limits on sole/last chain models
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1066` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +195
- **Deletions**: -11
- **Created**: 2026-09-29T09:41:51Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-29T21:12:07Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1066

## Change
When a retryable error yields a retry delay `D > policy.maxWait`, the engine used to `_failOver` — and with no next chain entry the whole chain died in <1s on a transient 429, with the `retriesPerEntry` budget untouched.

- **Fallback exists** (untried + not cooling): instant failover, byte-identical to before.
- **Sole/last eligible entry**: wait out the rate limit instead of exhausting — bounded by the new `retry.maxWaitForLastEntryMs` (default 5m, matching the existing `maxWait` default) so a pathological `Retry-After` (hours) still ends the chain. Waits `min(D, maxWaitForLastEntry)`.
- **Budget**: the wait-out goes through `_sleepAndRetry`, so it consumes `retriesPerEntry` attempts like any paid retry; the chain still exhausts when attempts run out.
- **Stream stays live** during the wait via the existing sleeper machinery (no new timer system); the wait-out announces through the normal `FallbackNoticeKind.retry` notice.
- **Exhaustion story** now reports the waited total: `... failed after 3 attempt(s) over 600s (waited 10m on rate limits).`

New config knob (one field, `retry:` section conventions): `maxWaitForLastEntryMs` in `ModelRolesRetryPolicy` (ctor + yaml parse + serialize round-trip), documented in the CLI help `retry:` section.

## Test evidence
`dart test test/model_roles/` — 194 tests, all passed (0baf52 worktree run), including:

- NEW `sole entry waits out a Retry-After beyond maxWait (issue #1066)` — 429 + `Retry-After: 60s`, `maxWait: 30s` → sleeps exactly 60s, retries, succeeds on attempt 2 (fake clock/sleeper).
- NEW `a pathological Retry-After waits out the ceiling, then exhausts (issue #1066)` — `Retry-After: 2h`, `maxWait: 30s` → two bounded 5m sleeps, budget spent, exhaustion message contains `waited 10m on rate limits`.
- NEW `the last eligible entry waits out even after an instant failover (issue #1066)` — A (10m wall) instant-fails over to B, B (60s wall, no fallback left) waits out and succeeds.
- Pinned: existing `a Retry-After beyond maxWait fails over instead of sleeping` stays green (multi-entry failover unchanged); `cooldown-wall exhaustion` test updated to reach the same cooldown-wall story through the new wait-out flow (ceiling 30s < 10m wall).

Also green: `dart analyze` clean on changed files; `test/cli/cli_help_test.dart`, `test/cli/cli_config_test.dart`, `test/skills/fa_self_config_accuracy_test.dart` (284 tests) all pass. No new dependencies.

- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.

  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only

  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1070
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1070
- **Title**: fix(#1066): wait out transient rate limits on sole/last chain models
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1066` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +195
- **Deletions**: -11
- **Created**: 2026-09-29T09:41:51Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-29T21:12:07Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1066

## Change
When a retryable error yields a retry delay `D > policy.maxWait`, the engine used to `_failOver` — and with no next chain entry the whole chain died in <1s on a transient 429, with the `retriesPerEntry` budget untouched.

- **Fallback exists** (untried + not cooling): instant failover, byte-identical to before.
- **Sole/last eligible entry**: wait out the rate limit instead of exhausting — bounded by the new `retry.maxWaitForLastEntryMs` (default 5m, matching the existing `maxWait` default) so a pathological `Retry-After` (hours) still ends the chain. Waits `min(D, maxWaitForLastEntry)`.
- **Budget**: the wait-out goes through `_sleepAndRetry`, so it consumes `retriesPerEntry` attempts like any paid retry; the chain still exhausts when attempts run out.
- **Stream stays live** during the wait via the existing sleeper machinery (no new timer system); the wait-out announces through the normal `FallbackNoticeKind.retry` notice.
- **Exhaustion story** now reports the waited total: `... failed after 3 attempt(s) over 600s (waited 10m on rate limits).`

New config knob (one field, `retry:` section conventions): `maxWaitForLastEntryMs` in `ModelRolesRetryPolicy` (ctor + yaml parse + serialize round-trip), documented in the CLI help `retry:` section.

## Test evidence
`dart test test/model_roles/` — 194 tests, all passed (0baf52 worktree run), including:

- NEW `sole entry waits out a Retry-After beyond maxWait (issue #1066)` — 429 + `Retry-After: 60s`, `maxWait: 30s` → sleeps exactly 60s, retries, succeeds on attempt 2 (fake clock/sleeper).
- NEW `a pathological Retry-After waits out the ceiling, then exhausts (issue #1066)` — `Retry-After: 2h`, `maxWait: 30s` → two bounded 5m sleeps, budget spent, exhaustion message contains `waited 10m on rate limits`.
- NEW `the last eligible entry waits out even after an instant failover (issue #1066)` — A (10m wall) instant-fails over to B, B (60s wall, no fallback left) waits out and succeeds.
- Pinned: existing `a Retry-After beyond maxWait fails over instead of sleeping` stays green (multi-entry failover unchanged); `cooldown-wall exhaustion` test updated to reach the same cooldown-wall story through the new wait-out flow (ceiling 30s < 10m wall).

Also green: `dart analyze` clean on changed files; `test/cli/cli_help_test.dart`, `test/cli/cli_config_test.dart`, `test/skills/fa_self_config_accuracy_test.dart` (284 tests) all pass. No new dependencies.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`
  (four modes — `sequence` equal-width slots, `duration` with idle gaps
  compressed out, `time` zero-width wall-clock markers, `actual` real gaps;
  three fixed lanes: 0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools),
  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),
  and `ThrottledTrajectorySearchIndex` (full-text; matches are stable
  record ids). `formatters.dart` holds the shared duration/token/throughput
  formatting; `trajectory_preview.dart` the bounded single-line previews;
  `trajectory_export.dart` the whole-snapshot JSON/Markdown exporters the
  header's copy menu uses. Tool records carry `startedAt` (real launch
  time, distinct from the projected position) so the Gantt/actual
  projections plot true spans. Outbound model requests persist for the
  ledger …

Now let me check the existing test that was pinned — `a Retry-After beyond maxWait fails over instead of sleeping` — to verify the multi-entry failover is unchanged.

Let me also examine the key logic more carefully for correctness issues:

1. **`_onNoCredential` path with `wait > policy.maxWait`**: Now goes to `_onExcessiveWait`. If no fallback available, waits `min(wait, maxWaitForLastEntry)` via `_sleepAndRetry`. Note: `_onNoCredential` is called when `credential == null` — every key is benched. Note there's a guard: `if (state.attemptsOnEntry >= policy.retriesPerEntry) return _failOver(...)` before. OK.

2. **`_onRetryable` path**: `delay > policy.maxWait` → `_onExcessiveWait`. If no fallback: `_sleepAndRetry` with bounded delay. Note `_sleepAndRetry` increments `attemptsOnEntry`, and there's a check before: `if (state.attemptsOnEntry >= policy.retriesPerEntry) return _failOver(out, state);` — hmm, wait. Look at the flow in `_onRetryable`:

```dart
if (state.attemptsOnEntry >= policy.retriesPerEntry) {
  return _failOver(out, state);
}
final delay = _retryDelay(state.attemptsOnEntry + 1, outcome.retryAfter);
if (delay > policy.maxWait) {
  return _onExcessiveWait(...);
}
```

Now `_failOver` can return `true` (moved to next entry) or `false` (chain exhausted → forwarded last failure). When `_failOver` returns true, the loop continues with next entry.

`_onExcessiveWait` when no fallback is available: `_sleepAndRetry(bounded)`. `_sleepAndRetry` increments `attemptsOnEntry`. So each wait-out consumes one retry. That matches the description.

3. **Potential issue: `_hasAvailableFallback` vs `_failOver`'s actual selection.** `_hasAvailableFallback(state.tried)` checks any entry NOT in `tried` and NOT in cooldown. But `_failOver` calls `_failover(...)` which does exactly the same loop: `if (tried.contains(index)) continue; if (isInCooldown(index)) continue;`. So the check mirrors failover's selection. BUT — there's a subtlety: `_failover` in queue mode (queueState != null) records failure into queue state and marks cooldown on `from`, then picks the next available. `_hasAvailableFallback` doesn't record anything, and importantly `_onExcessiveWait` calls `_failOver` directly if a fallback exists, so `_failover` runs then. When no fallback available, `_onExcessiveWait` waits instead of failing over — but in queue mode `_failover` is never called in that path, so `queueState.recordFailure(from, ...)` is NOT called and the cooldown for the entry is NOT recorded... Hmm wait, but actually in the wait-out path the entry is retried in place, so recording a failure may not be needed? Actually in queue mode each retryable failure... let me check: in queue mode with a fallback, `_failover` records the failure. In the wait-out path (no fallback), `_sleepAndRetry` is called directly, so no `recordFailure` and no cooldown marking. Is that a behavior change for the queue mode? In queue mode, cooldown marking on the failed entry happens through `_failover`. Now, before this change, on sole-entry excessive wait, `_failOver` would be called, which would record the failure and mark cooldown and then return null → forward last failure. Now, the wait-out path skips `recordFailure` — meaning the queue health (`consecutiveFailures`, `lastError`) doesn't see the failure. Hmm, but then subsequent retries of the same entry — on eventual exhaustion via budget, `_failOver` → `_failover` records failure once. So the failure count would be undercounted in queue mode for the wait-out scenario. Minor. Actually wait — in the wait-out path with retriesPerEntry budget spent, `_onRetryable` checks `attemptsOnEntry >= retriesPerEntry` → `_failOver` → records. But the intermediate failures (the ones that led to wait-outs) are not recorded into queue health. In roles mode, queueState is null so it doesn't matter. Queue mode (issue #418) — is this a real regression? Let's think: queue mode is used by the provider queue (`/model` queue feature?). The pre-existing behavior for a retryable error with `delay <= maxWait` also goes through `_sleepAndRetry` without `recordFailure` — so intermediate paid retries were never recorded in queue health either. Only the failover records. So the wait-out path behaves like a paid retry (not recording) — consistent with existing behavior for retries. Actually wait, but cooldown marking matters: previously on excessive wait with no fallback, `_failover` would mark the entry's cooldown (so a next call starts elsewhere or at least the entry is benched). Now, on wait-out exhaustion, the budget-spent path eventually calls `_failOver` → `_failover` marks cooldown. So cooldown still gets marked on exhaustion. OK.

But there's one more subtle scenario: in queue mode, `_hasAvailableFallback(state.tried)` — `tried` is per-call. In queue mode with the sticky cursor, `_DriveState` starts at `_firstAvailableIndex()` and `tried = {entryIndex}`. If failover happens (say entry 0 → entry 1), tried={0,1}. If entry 1 then has excessive wait, `_hasAvailableFallback` checks any entry not in tried and not in cooldown — entry 0 is in tried → skip. So no fallback → wait out. OK.

Now consider: entry 0 fails with excessive wait, has fallback entry 1 (not cooling) → `_failOver`. `_failover` marks entry 0 cooldown = retryAfter (10m). Then entry 1 gets excessive wait too, no fallback (entry 0 tried) → wait out bounded. Fine.

4. **`_hasAvailableFallback` cooldown check race**: `isInCooldown(index)` has a side effect: it removes the cooldown entry when expired (`_cooldownUntil.remove(index)`). That's fine, just lazy cleanup.

5. **The `waitedTotal` is incremented in `_sleepAndRetry` after the sleep** — only if the sleep completes without abort. If aborted, we don't count it (story not reported anyway since aborted path pushes `_pushAborted`). Good.

6. **Potential issue: `waitedTotal` counts ALL sleeps, including regular backoff retries, not just rate-limit wait-outs.** The exhaustion story says "waited X on rate limits" but `waitedTotal` accumulates every `_sleepAndRetry` delay — including transport retries (`isTransport: true`) and normal exponential backoff retries. So the message "waited 10m on rate limits" could be misleading: e.g., a chain that spent 300s waiting on transport retries and 0 on rate limits would report "(waited 5m on rate limits)". This is a correctness-of-message issue. Hmm — is that a big deal? The story says "waited ... on rate limits" — but transports also sleep. Let me double check `_sleepAndRetry` is used for transport retries: yes, `_onRetryable` calls `_sleepAndRetry(..., isTransport: outcome.isTransport)`. So transport retry sleeps increment waitedTotal too. And regular rate-limit backoff sleeps (under maxWait) also increment. So `waitedTotal` = total sleep time across all retry kinds. The label "on rate limits" is thus inaccurate for transport-only scenarios. It's a message-accuracy SUGGESTION/IMPORTANT. Let me think about how visible it is: the exhaustion story is an error message shown to the user. A transport-outage chain that waits 5m via retries would say "waited 5m on rate limits" — factually wrong and could mislead the user's diagnosis. I'd rate this IMPORTANT (message correctness) or SUGGESTION. Given the field doc says "Total time slept for retries in this call (the exhaustion story reports it)" — the doc itself is honest, but the story text says "on rate limits". I'd flag as IMPORTANT with a suggested fix: either rename the text to "(waited Xs retrying)" or track separately. Hmm, but severity guidance: BLOCKING = merge would cause a bug... This is a misleading diagnostic message, not a functional bug. IMPORTANT seems right.

Wait, actually let me reconsider. Also `waitedTotal` in the test "cooldown-wall exhaustion" case: the sleeps there... The updated test sets `maxWaitForLastEntry: 30s` and expects the same story. Fine.

7. **Test "a pathological Retry-After waits out the ceiling, then exhausts"**: retryAfter 2h, maxWait 30s, default retriesPerEntry 2, maxWaitForLastEntry default 5m. Flow: attempt 1 → rate limit → `_onRetryable`: attemptsOnEntry=0 < 2 → delay = 2h > 30s → `_onExcessiveWait` → no fallback → bounded = min(2h, 5m) = 5m → `_sleepAndRetry` → attemptsOnEntry=1, sleep 5m. Attempt 2 → rate limit → attemptsOnEntry=1 < 2 → delay 2h > maxWait → `_onExcessiveWait` → sleep 5m → attemptsOnEntry=2. Attempt 3 → rate limit → attemptsOnEntry=2 >= 2 → `_failOver` → `_failover`: no untried entries → null → forward last failure. Story: attempts=3, waited = 10m. elapsed = 10m (plus trivial). Test expects `waited 10m on rate limits`. ✓. Two sleeps of 5m each ✓.

Hmm wait — there's something interesting: the cooldown marking. When exhausting via `_failOver` → `_failover` marks entry 0's cooldown = retryAfter = 2h. So the next call will find entry 0 cooling → `_firstAvailableIndex()` returns... all entries cooling → returns 0 anyway. And with a single entry, the next call attempt: `_drive` starts at entry 0 (cooldown ignored in roles mode, `_firstAvailableIndex` falls back to 0 when all cooling). It will attempt again. OK — roles mode doesn't die loud on all-cooling (that's queue mode only). Fine.

8. **Serialization round trip**: `toYaml` now includes `maxWaitForLastEntryMs`. `fromYaml` parses it. OK. Are there tests pinning `toYaml` output? Let me search for `maxWaitMs` in tests.

9. **CLI help test**: `test/cli_help_test.dart` — does it pin the exact help text? The PR says it passes. Let me verify the help text change is consistent — the help lists `maxWaitForLastEntryMs` in the retry comment. ✓.

10. **The `_onExcessiveWait` on the `_onNoCredential` path — double reason computation**: The code computes the reason string twice (`lastFailure == null ? 'all API keys in backoff' : _shortReasonText(lastFailure.error)` appears in both the `_onExcessiveWait` call and the `_sleepAndRetry` call below). Minor duplication — SUGGESTION.

11. **Potential issue: `_onNoCredential` wait-out doesn't respect key rotation budget... ** Actually `_onNoCredential` handles the all-keys-benched case. With the new wait-out, a sole entry whose key(s) are benched for 10m will now wait out `min(10m+1s, 5m)` = 5m, then retry... The bench remains (10m wall), so after 5m sleep the key is still benched → `_onNoCredential` again → attemptsOnEntry now 1... eventually exhausts budget → `_failOver` → forward. OK bounded.

But wait — there's a subtle issue with the multi-key ring case in `_onNoCredential`: `wait = earliestBackoffEnd + 1s`. Suppose two keys benched at different times: earliest frees in 60s. wait=61s > 30s maxWait. Previously → failover. Now (sole entry) → wait out 61s, re-select picks up the freed key. Good — that's the intent.

12. **`_hasAvailableFallback` ignores the current entry's cooldown for the wait-out decision** — fine.

13. **Edge: `maxWaitForLastEntry < maxWait` config.** E.g., user sets maxWait: 30s, maxWaitForLastEntry: 10s. Then bounded = min(delay, 10s). But the regular path (`delay <= maxWait`) can sleep up to maxWait (30s). So the "ceiling" for last entry is smaller than for mid-chain. Semantically fine — it's a ceiling, not a floor. But what if user sets `maxWaitForLastEntryMs: 0`? Then bounded = 0 → `_sleepAndRetry(0)` → immediate retry without sleep, consuming attempts. Busy-retry loop against a rate-limited provider — hammering with 0 delay. Hmm: `ms()` in fromYaml allows 0 (`value < 0` throws; 0 is allowed). With maxWaitForLastEntry=0, every excessive wait becomes an immediate retry until budget exhausts. retriesPerEntry default 2 → 3 hammering attempts. Bounded by budget, so not infinite. Minor footgun, worth a suggestion? The `waitedText` skips `inSeconds < 1`. Not a big deal. Also `maxWait: 0` similarly would make every retry go through `_onExcessiveWait`. That's pre-existing behavior for maxWait=0 (everything fails over). Now with maxWait=0 and sole entry: bounded = min(delay, 5m) — waits out. Fine, arguably better.

14. **Backward compat**: default `maxWaitForLastEntry` = 5m changes default behavior: a sole-entry chain that previously died in <1s now waits up to 5m per retry. That's the FIX itself (issue #1066 asks for it). Multi-entry chains with fallback available: unchanged (verified by `_hasAvailableFallback` check). But — what about multi-entry chains where all other entries are cooling? Previously: `_failOver` → `_failover` finds no available → forward last failure (die). Now: wait out. This is also the intent ("sole/last eligible"). OK.

15. One more: **`_onExcessiveWait` in the `_onNoCredential` path passes `isTransport: false` (default)**. In `_onNoCredential`, the failure could have been a transport failure... Actually `_onNoCredential` is about benched keys; the notice kind will be `retry` not `transportRetry`. Previously the same code called `_sleepAndRetry` directly with default isTransport: false. So unchanged. OK.

16. **`_hasAvailableFallback(state.tried)` in queue mode vs `_failover`'s `noCooldown` param**: `_onRetryable`'s `immediate` path (auth/budget) calls `_failOver(noCooldown: true)` directly, bypassing `_onExcessiveWait` — good, since immediate deaths shouldn't wait out.

Wait, actually, there IS a subtle case in `_onRetryable`: the `immediate` check happens BEFORE the maxWait check, so auth/budget deaths fail over (or exhaust) regardless. Good.

17. **The `waitedTotal` name/doc vs. what it measures**: covered in #6.

18. **Test coverage**: New tests cover sole entry wait-out, pathological ceiling exhaustion, last-eligible-after-failover. What about the `_onNoCredential` (all keys benched) wait-out path? Not covered by new tests, I think. Let me check if an existing test covers the no-credential + wait > maxWait path. The path `lastFailure == null ? 'all API keys in backoff'` — when is `lastFailure` null in `_onNoCredential`? When the call starts and every key is benched from a previous call (cooldown from earlier session activity). Existing tests may cover multi-key benching. A test for `_onExcessiveWait` via the no-credential path (e.g., single entry, key benched 10m from a prior call, second call arrives) would be good. Let me search the test file.

19. **`_etaText` for waited**: `_etaText(waited)` — for 600s gives "10m". For 90s → "1m" (inMinutes >= 1 → 1m). Slight rounding: 90s shows "1m". Eh, matches existing cooldown ETA style. Fine.

20. **`state.waitedTotal += delay` placement**: after the sleep completes. In the abort case the story isn't reported (aborted), so no issue.

21. **Docs**: The PR says "documented in the CLI help `retry:` section" — done. Is there a docs/ page about model roles that should mention the new knob? Let me check docs/ for model roles config documentation.

Let me also check whether `cli_help_test.dart` pins the full text (the PR says it passes; the help test may check for the presence of lines). Let me check if any test pins `toYaml()` round-trip for the policy — search tests for `maxWaitMs`.

22. Another potential issue: **`_hasAvailableFallback` treats the current entry itself**: if `tried` contains only the current entry and the current entry is NOT in cooldown (it just failed with retryable error — in roles mode, no cooldown is marked until failover), other entries checked. The current entry is in tried → skipped. Good.

23. **Interaction with `_failOver` marking cooldown**: In the wait-out path, the failing entry never gets its cooldown marked during waits (only on true exhaustion). So mid-wait, `currentModel` (used for display) still points at the cooling-less entry 0. Fine.

24. **Stream liveness**: The wait uses `_sleeper` with cancelToken — default sleeper wakes early on cancel. Good.

25. `waitedTotal` in queue mode: the exhaustion story with queue lines also prints waited. Fine.

Now the message-accuracy issue (#6) — let me weigh again. The scenario: sole entry, transport failures (connection reset) with exponential backoff capped at maxBackoff 8s; retriesPerEntry=2 → waits 0.5s + 1s (jitter) — tiny. For the waited text to be large with transports you'd need large Retry-After... transports don't carry retryAfter usually; `_retryDelay` for transport = backoffFor(attempt) capped at maxBackoff (default 8s). So transport-only chains accumulate ≤ ~8s * retriesPerEntry * entries... e.g., 3 entries × 2 retries × 8s ≈ 48s → "waited 48s on rate limits" — misleading for a pure transport outage. Also rate-limit backoffs under maxWait add up too (those ARE rate limits, fine). So the inaccuracy shows in mixed/transport scenarios. It's a wording bug in a user-facing diagnostic. I'll flag as IMPORTANT (low effort fix: accumulate only non-transport sleeps, or reword).

Hmm, wait — let me reconsider: is it worth IMPORTANT? "IMPORTANT — real maintainability or correctness issue." A factually wrong user-facing error message is a correctness issue of the message, not the mechanism. I'll keep it IMPORTANT but note it's minor.

26. Let me check the `_onNoCredential` change more carefully:

```dart
final lastFailure = state.lastFailure;
if (wait > policy.maxWait) {
  return _onExcessiveWait(
    out, state, wait,
    lastFailure == null ? 'all API keys in backoff' : _shortReasonText(lastFailure.error),
    cancelToken,

}
return _sleepAndRetry(
  out, state, wait,

```

Duplication of the reason ternary — could hoist. SUGGESTION.

27. In `_onRetryable`, `isTransport: outcome.isTransport` is passed to `_onExcessiveWait` — so a transport excessive-wait waits out with a `transportRetry` notice. Good consistency.

28. Potential subtle bug: **`_onExcessiveWait` checks `_hasAvailableFallback(state.tried)` — but `_failOver` may still return false** (chain exhausted) if between the check and the failover... no, single-threaded, same tick. But WAIT: `_failover` ALSO marks cooldown on `from` BEFORE looking for the next entry. `_hasAvailableFallback` checks entries not in tried and not in cooldown — this matches `_failover`'s selection loop exactly (`tried.contains(index) continue; isInCooldown(index) continue`). And marking `from`'s cooldown doesn't affect selection since `from ∈ tried`. So `_failOver` will find a target iff `_hasAvailableFallback` is true. Consistent.

30. **What if `retryAfter` is negative or zero?** `_retryDelay` returns retryAfter directly; `delay > maxWait` false → normal path. Fine.

31. What about the **`cooldown-wall exhaustion` test modification**: They changed the test to set `maxWaitForLastEntry: 30s`. The test previously relied on old behavior where excessive wait → failover → cooldowns. Now with the fix, the second entry would wait out (default 5m) making the test slow — hence the 30s ceiling. Reasonable. But note: the test now uses fake sleeper so no real time. OK.

32. **Missing test for the no-credential wait-out**: let me verify by searching the test file for `all API keys in backoff`.

33. **Docs update check**: docs/ folder — is there a model-roles doc listing retry knobs? Let me grep.

34. Also check `schema/` — is there a JSON schema for config with retry section? Let me check `schema/` for roles config schema.

35. Check `fa_self_config_accuracy_test.dart` mention — they ran it. Fine.

36. Also — **the class doc** mentions `maxWaitForLastEntry` — consistent naming.

37. `cli_help.dart` — help text wrapped fine.

38. One more possible issue: **`_onExcessiveWait` naming/param `delay`** vs `wait` naming in `_onNoCredential`. Trivial.

39. **Behavior change not covered by test**: multi-entry chain where entry A is sole-eligible because entry B is COOLING (not tried). Scenario: A fails with 60s Retry-After (maxWait 30s); B in cooldown 10m (benched earlier in the same call, in tried → actually if B was tried it's in tried). During the call, entries get cooling marks only via `_failover`. A fails excessive wait → `_hasAvailableFallback(tried={A})` → B: not tried, but `isInCooldown(B)` true → false → wait out. Correct: B is cooling so failover would find nothing... BUT `_failover` would mark A's cooldown and return null → forward last failure (die). Wait-out is the desired new behavior. ✓ consistent.

But subtle: B's cooldown could LAPSE during A's 5m wait-out. The wait-out decision is made once at decision time; after sleeping 5m, B may be healthy but the chain stays on A. That's fine — A is the primary.

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1070
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1070
- **Title**: fix(#1066): wait out transient rate limits on sole/last chain models
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1066` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +195
- **Deletions**: -11
- **Created**: 2026-09-29T09:41:51Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-29T21:12:07Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1066

## Change
When a retryable error yields a retry delay `D > policy.maxWait`, the engine used to `_failOver` — and with no next chain entry the whole chain died in <1s on a transient 429, with the `retriesPerEntry` budget untouched.

- **Fallback exists** (untried + not cooling): instant failover, byte-identical to before.
- **Sole/last eligible entry**: wait out the rate limit instead of exhausting — bounded by the new `retry.maxWaitForLastEntryMs` (default 5m, matching the existing `maxWait` default) so a pathological `Retry-After` (hours) still ends the chain. Waits `min(D, maxWaitForLastEntry)`.
- **Budget**: the wait-out goes through `_sleepAndRetry`, so it consumes `retriesPerEntry` attempts like any paid retry; the chain still exhausts when attempts run out.
- **Stream stays live** during the wait via the existing sleeper machinery (no new timer system); the wait-out announces through the normal `FallbackNoticeKind.retry` notice.
- **Exhaustion story** now reports the waited total: `... failed after 3 attempt(s) over 600s (waited 10m on rate limits).`

New config knob (one field, `retry:` section conventions): `maxWaitForLastEntryMs` in `ModelRolesRetryPolicy` (ctor + yaml parse + serialize round-trip), documented in the CLI help `retry:` section.

## Test evidence
`dart test test/model_roles/` — 194 tests, all passed (0baf52 worktree run), including:

- NEW `sole entry waits out a Retry-After beyond maxWait (issue #1066)` — 429 + `Retry-After: 60s`, `maxWait: 30s` → sleeps exactly 60s, retries, succeeds on attempt 2 (fake clock/sleeper).
- NEW `a pathological Retry-After waits out the ceiling, then exhausts (issue #1066)` — `Retry-After: 2h`, `maxWait: 30s` → two bounded 5m sleeps, budget spent, exhaustion message contains `waited 10m on rate limits`.
- NEW `the last eligible entry waits out even after an instant failover (issue #1066)` — A (10m wall) instant-fails over to B, B (60s wall, no fallback left) waits out and succeeds.
- Pinned: existing `a Retry-After beyond maxWait fails over instead of sleeping` stays green (multi-entry failover unchanged); `cooldown-wall exhaustion` test updated to reach the same cooldown-wall story through the new wait-out flow (ceiling 30s < 10m wall).

Also green: `dart analyze` clean on changed files; `test/cli/cli_help_test.dart`, `test/cli/cli_config_test.dart`, `test/skills/fa_self_config_accuracy_test.dart` (284 tests) all pass. No new dependencies.

- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build

  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`

  three fixed lanes: 0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools),
  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),
  and `ThrottledTrajectorySearchIndex` (full-text; matches are stable

  formatting; `trajectory_preview.dart` the bounded single-line previews;
  `trajectory_export.dart` the whole-snapshot JSON/Markdown exporters the
  header's copy menu uses. Tool records carry `startedAt` (real launch
  time, distinct from the projected position) so the Gantt/actual

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review"] O2["Write outputs/pr_review_general.md — brief general PR comment (1-2 paragraphs max)"] O3["Write ou…

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1070
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1070
- **Title**: fix(#1066): wait out transient rate limits on sole/last chain models
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1066` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +195
- **Deletions**: -11
- **Created**: 2026-09-29T09:41:51Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-29T21:12:07Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1066

## Change
When a retryable error yields a retry delay `D > policy.maxWait`, the engine used to `_failOver` — and with no next chain entry the whole chain died in <1s on a transient 429, with the `retriesPerEntry` budget untouched.

- **Fallback exists** (untried + not cooling): instant failover, byte-identical to before.
- **Sole/last eligible entry**: wait out the rate limit instead of exhausting — bounded by the new `retry.maxWaitForLastEntryMs` (default 5m, matching the existing `maxWait` default) so a pathological `Retry-After` (hours) still ends the chain. Waits `min(D, maxWaitForLastEntry)`.
- **Budget**: the wait-out goes through `_sleepAndRetry`, so it consumes `retriesPerEntry` attempts like any paid retry; the chain still exhausts when attempts run out.
- **Stream stays live** during the wait via the existing sleeper machinery (no new timer system); the wait-out announces through the normal `FallbackNoticeKind.retry` notice.
- **Exhaustion story** now reports the waited total: `... failed after 3 attempt(s) over 600s (waited 10m on rate limits).`

New config knob (one field, `retry:` section conventions): `maxWaitForLastEntryMs` in `ModelRolesRetryPolicy` (ctor + yaml parse + serialize round-trip), documented in the CLI help `retry:` section.

## Test evidence
`dart test test/model_roles/` — 194 tests, all passed (0baf52 worktree run), including:

- NEW `sole entry waits out a Retry-After beyond maxWait (issue #1066)` — 429 + `Retry-After: 60s`, `maxWait: 30s` → sleeps exactly 60s, retries, succeeds on attempt 2 (fake clock/sleeper).
- NEW `a pathological Retry-After waits out the ceiling, then exhausts (issue #1066)` — `Retry-After: 2h`, `maxWait: 30s` → two bounded 5m sleeps, budget spent, exhaustion message contains `waited 10m on rate limits`.
- NEW `the last eligible entry waits out even after an instant failover (issue #1066)` — A (10m wall) instant-fails over to B, B (60s wall, no fallback left) waits out and succeeds.
- Pinned: existing `a Retry-After beyond maxWait fails over instead of sleeping` stays green (multi-entry failover unchanged); `cooldown-wall exhaustion` test updated to reach the same cooldown-wall story through the new wait-out flow (ceiling 30s < 10m wall).

Also green: `dart analyze` clean on changed files; `test/cli/cli_help_test.dart`, `test/cli/cli_config_test.dart`, `test/skills/fa_self_config_accuracy_test.dart` (284 tests) all pass. No new dependencies.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`
  (four modes — `sequence` equal-width slots, `duration` with idle gaps
  compressed out, `time` zero-width wall-clock markers, `actual` real gaps;
  three fixed lanes: 0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools),
  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),
  and `ThrottledTrajectorySearchIndex` (full-text; matches are stable
  record ids). `formatters.dart` holds the shared duration/token/throughput
  formatting; `trajectory_preview.dart` the bounded single-line previews;
  `trajectory_export.dart` the whole-snapshot JSON/Markdown exporters the
  header's copy menu uses. Tool records carry `startedAt` (real launch
  time, distinct from the projected position) so the Gantt/actual
  projections plot true spans. Outbound model requests persist for the
  ledger …
